youtube.title: Suwalki Gap Explained: The 65 km Strip Holding the Baltic States to NATO
youtube.description:
The Suwalki Gap is a strip of Polish-Lithuanian border about 65 km across, and it is the only land link between NATO and the Baltic states of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania. Squeezed between Russia's Kaliningrad and Belarus, it is the narrowest door in the alliance. Why is it so narrow, and why can nobody widen it? We measure the gap on the map, follow the borders of 1920, 1945, 1991 and 2004 that created it, and look at what NATO and Russia each say.

On the map we measure the gap today, follow the four borders of 1920, 1945, 1991 and 2004 that left it behind, set out what NATO and Russia each say about it, and look at three ways it could change: fortified borders, a Baltic Sea ringed by NATO, and a new railway.

{CHAPTERS}

sources.claim: Kaliningrad and Belarus are about 65 km apart across the Polish-Lithuanian border
sources.source: Hodges, Bugajski, Doran, 'Securing the Suwałki Corridor', CEPA, July 2018; BBC News, June 2022 ('65km, 40 miles')

sources.claim: About six million people live in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania
sources.source: Eurostat population on 1 January 2024: EE 1.37m, LV 1.87m, LT 2.89m

sources.claim: The Poland-Lithuania border is about 104 km long
sources.source: State Border Guard Service of Lithuania, border data

sources.claim: Kaliningrad has about one million people
sources.source: Rosstat, 2021 All-Russian census: Kaliningrad oblast 1,029,966

sources.claim: Transit between Kaliningrad and the rest of Russia through Lithuania under a 2002 deal
sources.source: Joint Statement of the EU and the Russian Federation on transit between the Kaliningrad region and the rest of the Russian Federation, 11 November 2002

sources.claim: Baltiysk is the main base of Russia's Baltic Fleet
sources.source: Russian Ministry of Defence, Baltic Fleet page

sources.claim: Belarus and Russia joined in the Union State treaty in 1999
sources.source: Treaty on the Creation of a Union State, signed 8 December 1999

sources.claim: Grodno lies about 20 km from the Polish border
sources.source: Measured on OpenStreetMap, Grodno to the Kuźnica crossing

sources.claim: Suwałki has about 69,000 people
sources.source: Statistics Poland (GUS), National Census 2021

sources.claim: Budzisko-Kalvarija is the Via Baltica crossing toward Kaunas and Riga
sources.source: European Commission TEN-T North Sea-Baltic corridor maps; Polish S61 expressway (GDDKiA)

sources.claim: One railway crossing at Trakiszki-Mockava
sources.source: Lithuanian Railways (LTG) and PKP PLK network maps

sources.claim: Poland's rails are 1,435 mm apart, Lithuania's 1,520 mm
sources.source: Rail Baltica project documentation; UIC gauge standards

sources.claim: Since 2015 a European-gauge line runs from the Polish border to Kaunas
sources.source: Rail Baltica / Lithuanian Railways, opening of the Kaunas-Polish border 1,435 mm line, 2015

sources.claim: Vilnius is about 30 km from the Belarusian border
sources.source: Measured on OpenStreetMap; Lithuanian government statements cite about 30-35 km

sources.claim: Suwałki Agreement signed 7 October 1920, in Suwałki
sources.source: Suwałki Agreement text, League of Nations Treaty Series; Encyclopaedia Britannica

sources.claim: Vilnius lies about 165 km east of Suwałki
sources.source: Measured on OpenStreetMap, Suwałki town centre to Vilnius old town, straight line

sources.claim: Two days later Polish troops under General Żeligowski took Vilnius
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Lithuania: Interwar period'; Vilnius taken 9 October 1920

sources.claim: Poland held Vilnius until 1939; diplomatic relations established in 1938
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica; Polish ultimatum of 17 March 1938

sources.claim: Potsdam Conference, August 1945, agreed in principle to the transfer of Königsberg and the adjacent area to the USSR
sources.source: Protocol of the Proceedings of the Berlin (Potsdam) Conference, 2 August 1945, section VI ('agreed in principle to the proposal of the Soviet Government concerning the ultimate transfer... pending the final determination of territorial questions at the peace settlement')

sources.claim: Southern East Prussia went under Polish administration
sources.source: Potsdam Protocol, 2 August 1945, section IX(b)

sources.claim: Polish-Soviet border treaty of 16 August 1945
sources.source: Treaty between Poland and the USSR concerning the Polish-Soviet State Frontier, Moscow, 16 August 1945

sources.claim: Königsberg renamed Kaliningrad in July 1946; most remaining Germans deported by 1948
sources.source: Decree of the Presidium of the Supreme Soviet, 4 July 1946; Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Kaliningrad'

sources.claim: On 6 September 1991 Moscow recognised the independence of Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia
sources.source: Resolution of the USSR State Council, 6 September 1991

sources.claim: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania had been taken into the Soviet Union in 1940
sources.source: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Baltic states: Soviet occupation', 1940

sources.claim: The Soviet Union ended in December 1991
sources.source: Declaration 142-N of the Soviet of the Republics, 26 December 1991

sources.claim: Belarus was independent by the end of 1991
sources.source: Declaration of State Independence of the Byelorussian SSR, 25 August 1991; Belovezha Accords, 8 December 1991

sources.claim: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania joined NATO on 29 March 2004; Poland on 12 March 1999
sources.source: NATO, 'Member countries'

sources.claim: A UN vote backed by 100 countries called the Crimea annexation invalid
sources.source: UN General Assembly Resolution 68/262, 27 March 2014 (100 in favour, 11 against, 58 abstentions)

sources.claim: RAND war games: Russian forces reached Tallinn or Riga within 36 to 60 hours
sources.source: Shlapak and Johnson, 'Reinforcing Deterrence on NATO's Eastern Flank', RAND Corporation, 2016

sources.claim: NATO's Warsaw summit agreed four multinational battlegroups
sources.source: Warsaw Summit Communiqué, NATO, 9 July 2016

sources.claim: The US-led battlegroup in Poland is based at Orzysz, about 70 km south-west of Suwałki
sources.source: NATO Multinational Corps Northeast, eFP Battlegroup Poland; distance measured on OpenStreetMap

sources.claim: Germany formally set up a permanent armoured brigade in Lithuania on 1 April 2025, aiming for about 4,800 soldiers by 2027
sources.source: Bundeswehr, Panzerbrigade 45 commissioning, 1 April 2025; German Federal Ministry of Defence

sources.claim: Germany's first permanent brigade abroad since the Second World War
sources.source: German Federal Ministry of Defence and Bundeswehr statements on Panzerbrigade 45, 1 April 2025 (the first Bundeswehr brigade permanently stationed outside Germany)

sources.claim: Poland announced East Shield in May 2024, about 10 billion złoty through 2028
sources.source: Polish Ministry of National Defence, announcement 18 May 2024

sources.claim: 10 billion złoty is roughly 2.5 billion dollars at 2024 exchange rates
sources.source: Our conversion of the Polish MoD figure (18 May 2024) at about 4 złoty per US dollar, National Bank of Poland reference rate, May 2024 (about 3.9-4.0)

sources.claim: Poland spent 4.1% of GDP on defence in 2024; Estonia 3.4%, Latvia 3.2%, Lithuania 2.9%; target 2%; no NATO member spent a larger share
sources.source: NATO, 'Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries (2014-2024)', 17 June 2024 (estimates; Poland highest at 4.12%)

sources.claim: Russia's December 2021 drafts asked NATO to stop expanding and pull back forces deployed since 1997
sources.source: Russian Foreign Ministry, draft Agreement on measures to ensure the security of Russia and NATO member states, published 17 December 2021, Articles 4 and 6

sources.claim: In June 2022 Lithuania stopped EU-sanctioned goods such as steel crossing to Kaliningrad by rail
sources.source: Lithuanian Railways and Lithuanian Foreign Ministry, 18 June 2022; Reuters, June 2022

sources.claim: Moscow called the move hostile and said it reserved the right to act to protect its interests
sources.source: Russian Foreign Ministry statement, 21 June 2022, as reported by Reuters

sources.claim: Rail transit resumed in July 2022 after EU guidance
sources.source: European Commission guidance on Kaliningrad transit, 13 July 2022; Reuters, 23 July 2022

sources.claim: In March 2023 Russia announced it would station tactical nuclear weapons in Belarus
sources.source: Vladimir Putin, interview on Rossiya-1, 25 March 2023

sources.claim: Lukashenko said in June 2023 that the first warheads had arrived
sources.source: Alexander Lukashenko, interview on Rossiya-1, June 2023, as reported by Reuters

sources.claim: Zapad 2017: Russia and Belarus declared 12,700 troops; Baltic officials warned of up to 100,000
sources.source: Russian and Belarusian defence ministries, notification under the Vienna Document, 2017; Lithuanian and Estonian defence officials quoted by Reuters, 2017

sources.claim: Article 5, in short: an attack on one member is an attack on all (paraphrase; treaty text: 'an armed attack against one or more of them in Europe or North America shall be considered an attack against them all')
sources.source: North Atlantic Treaty, Article 5, 4 April 1949

sources.claim: Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania agreed a joint Baltic Defence Line in January 2024
sources.source: Agreement of Baltic defence ministers, Riga, 19 January 2024

sources.claim: Finland joined NATO in April 2023 and Sweden in March 2024
sources.source: NATO: Finland 4 April 2023, Sweden 7 March 2024

sources.claim: Gotland lies about 300 km from Kaliningrad's coast
sources.source: Measured on OpenStreetMap, southern Gotland to Baltiysk

sources.claim: Rail Baltica's Baltic section is about 870 km, main line targeted for 2030
sources.source: RB Rail AS, Rail Baltica project facts, 2024

sources.claim: European auditors reported delays and rising costs on Rail Baltica
sources.source: European Court of Auditors, Special Report 10/2020 on EU transport infrastructures
